input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The sync wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across calls, so concurrent threads calling the same decorated function corrupt each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at once. Mechanism: stats.clear() and the shared dict assignment on lines 377-379 let both calls write to the same dict, which the original per-call copy.statistics avoided. Impact: stats such as attempt_number are interleaved or reset, giving silently wrong values.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism: one statistics dict is cleared and reused instead of being created per call, so concurrent threads calling the same decorated function wipe and interleave each other's stats such as attempt_number. It mentions only the sync wrapper and not the async case, but the faulty operation and the way it fails are the same.
